column47: The Department of Anthropology Ph.D. program at the University of California, Irvine focuses on social and cultural anthropology. [3] Graduate training in anthropology involves a period of long-term, independent fieldwork, generally (though not always) outside the United States, and often conducted in a language other than English. [3] Attentive to our discipline's past and indeed the paradigm of disciplinarity that has structured social inquiry since the early 20th century, our program gives students a breadth of knowledge in traditional anthropology and the traditional subjects of anthropological study. [6] At the same time, we push the boundaries of the discipline and use our ethnographic work to stretch the anthropological imagination. [6] The department provides students with superb training in both theory and method. [3] Areas of teaching emphasis include: the anthropology of modernity and development; political, legal, and economic anthropology; ethnographic method; and the anthropology of science, technology, and medicine. [3] The program involves three years of course work, with the bulk of requirements typically satisfied after the first two. The third year focuses on developing a research proposal and advancing to candidacy. [3] The fourth and often part of the fifth year are for extended anthropological fieldwork, and the sixth year is for writing the dissertation. [3] The department is committed to fostering new and innovative approaches to anthropological inquiry in a pluralistic and intellectually open academic environment. [3, 6]

column47: The Master of Arts (M.A.) in Comparative Literature combines the objectives of graduate study in foreign languages and literatures with an emphasis on the intercultural and international aspects of literature. The goal of the program is to provide graduate-t-level raining [sic]in subjects common to more than one national literature. Research work in the program is directed toward the analysis of cultural, historical, literary, linguistic, ethical and social concerns in literature, as approached through comparative methods of analysis informed by literary and cultural theory, as well as theories and practices from a variety of disciplines including psychology, sociology, anthropology, history and others. Because of the benefits of reading literature in the original language, the M.A. program requires students to have sufficient proficiency in at least one foreign language to take graduate literature seminars in that language. The M.A. in Comparative Literature is of particular value for students who intend to pursue a doctoral degree in comparative literature or in a foreign language and literature, or who plan to teach literature at the K-12 or community college levels. Some upper-division courses in Comparative and World Literature (CWL) or English (taken as part of the degree program electives) may apply to subject matter preparation for the Single Subject Teaching Credential in English (CWL Emphasis). For information about the Teaching Credential, please consult the Credentials Office in the College of Education.

column47: The Master of Fine Arts (M.F.A.) in Dance at the University of California, Irvine is an intensive, interdisciplinary two-year program that integrates studio practice with academic research. [12] Students engage in an educational experience where performance, creative exploration, and scholarly inquiry are deeply interconnected. [12] The program is designed to expand a student's artistic voice and prepare them for a lasting impact across dance, the arts, education, technology, and cultural engagement. [14] Over the two years of study, students take a variety of classroom and studio courses, with attention to connecting the mind and the body, expanding dance literacy and skills, and fostering creativity in new choreographic work. [13] In the second year, students focus on a culminating thesis project, which may take the form of creative projects or written research in a range of areas, including choreography, dance pedagogy, dance media and technology, dance training, dance science, and dance studies. [12, 14] Graduates of the program have entered diverse job markets, securing college and university faculty positions, starting their own dance companies, or pursuing Ph.D. degrees. [13]

The program is designed to encourage students to develop a unique body of research working closely with a small group of faculty at both UCI and UCSD. Students can also pursue interdisciplinary certificates in areas such as Asian American studies, Chicano/Latino Studies, Critical Theory, Gender and Sexuality Studies, Latin American Studies, Medical Humanities, Rhetoric and Composition, and Visual Studies. The program structure allows students to customize their studies around their intellectual interests. Students typically spend the first two years taking a minimum of 15 graduate seminars, fulfilling a foreign language requirement with a reading knowledge of one foreign language, and completing an M.A. paper. [3, 4] The third year is dedicated to preparing for qualifying exams in two or three fields of study, which are designed in consultation with a faculty advisor. [3, 4] Following the successful completion of these exams, students proceed to write a dissertation under the guidance of a three-person committee. [3, 4] The program aims to provide students with a variety of topics, approaches, genres, and theoretical issues in literary history, while also preparing them for an area of specialization. [4]

column47: The PhD a chemistry a se oferi în primul rând un grad de cercetare. Acesta este acordat studenților care au demonstrat competență în planificarea și desfășurarea cercetării originale în domeniul chimiei, au demonstrat o familiaritate largă cu știința chimiei, înțelegere în aplicarea metodei științifice și au dobândit o cunoaștere aprofundată a domeniului lor de specializare. Studenții își construiesc o bază solidă în toate cele patru domenii de bază ale chimiei (analitică, anorganică, organică și fizică) și o cunoaștere aprofundată a domeniului de specializare ales. În prima parte a programului de doctorat, studenții urmează cel puțin un curs formal în fiecare dintre domeniile de bază ale chimiei, așa cum este prezentat în cerințele de curs de mai jos. Cursurile trebuie finalizate cu succes (B- sau mai bine) până la sfârșitul celui de-al treilea semestru. Deoarece cercetarea originală este cerința principală pentru diploma de doctorat, un student își alege un supervizor de cercetare și începe cercetarea înainte de sfârșitul primului an. Studentul și supervizorul de cercetare selectează apoi doi membri ai facultății pentru a servi ca Comitet de Cercetare Doctorală al studentului. Comitetul, în colaborare cu consilierul de cercetare al studentului, preia funcția de consiliere de la comitetul de absolvenți și ghidează activitatea studentului pentru a promova dezvoltarea ca investigator independent. Astfel, în plus față de cercetare, fiecare student trebuie să îndeplinească următoarele cerințe: Serviciu ca asistent didactic; Actualizări regulate ale progresului cu un Comitet de Cercetare al facultății; Un seminar departamental; Susținerea unei propuneri de cercetare originale. column47: The Master of Conservation and Restoration Science (MCRS) is designed for professionals or recent graduates who wish to further their education and gain skills that will help them obtain or advance in careers related to environmental management. [3] The MCRS program integrates academic scholarship in ecology and evolutionary biology, training in natural resource management and stewardship, professional development (leadership training in agency, non-profit and for-profit conservation), and community engagement (translational partnerships in research and education). [3] Upon completion of the program, graduates are able to lead and collaborate in the planning, design, implementation, and management of complex, large-scale environmental conservation and restoration activities, in agency, non-profit, and for-profit settings. [1, 3] MCRS graduates have the broad knowledge in applied ecosystem and community ecology, in addition to training in the use of Geographical Information Systems (GIS) and informatics (data analysis and management). [1, 3] This two-year program of study consists of a four-part curriculum: a first-year sequence of core topic and professional development courses, a summer research/policy internship, a second-year of elective courses, and a team-based capstone experience (that serves as the thesis project). [1, 3] The summer internship and capstone experience are focused on stakeholder-engaged scholarship with community partners, where students are embedded in real-world conservation and restoration settings.
